Wide painted landscape, low worm's-eye angle from the valley floor. A great jade-green mountain ridge with a single deep, narrow cleft running down its centre between two rounded shoulders of rock, pines along the rims. Out of a deep ultramarine #1e4d9c sky a single enormous column of white luminous cloud plunges down and pushes deep into the cleft, filling the gorge to the brim, mist surging back out over both shoulders of the ridge in slow heavy rolls, pines bent all one way by the push. At the foot of the cleft a hot spring has burst from the rock, a thin white plume of steam. Violet #c084fc light glows along the wet rims of the ridge where the cloud presses against it. Rain streaks drift upward. One hard break of low gold light from the side. Huge, slow, sensual landscape. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
